justification: Changes what a paid Intelligence Brief tells the reader when a field is empty. The per-field renderer computed a plain-English explanation and then discarded it, showing only a two-word label — so 'None here' could not be distinguished from 'we never checked' or 'the lookup broke'. That is the absence-versus-failure ambiguity the surrounding campaign exists to remove. The classifier is also extracted into its own module so its wording is unit-testable. No database read or write, no migration, no schema change, no new external call, no change to what any pipeline computes.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any branch of describeUnavailable returns a detail that is empty, shorter than five words, or identical to its own label — i.e. a label with no explanation behind it. Verified by rewriting the not-requested branch's detail to the bare string 'Not included': two assertions went red (2 failed / 7 passed) and both returned green once the sentence was restored.

pre_impl.existing_data: No stored data is read or written. The change is entirely at render time over sections already streamed to the page, plus a file move of a pure function. No property_reports row, no database, no API contract is touched.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The per-field branch assumed a short status label was enough for an empty field. Every other caller of describeUnavailable — the section header, market context, and the Data Gaps list — already renders the detail sentence, so the field grid was the sole place the explanation was computed and dropped.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reuses describeUnavailable rather than writing new copy: all wording already existed and is unchanged. The extraction into unavailable.ts follows the pattern main already established with provenance.ts, and SECTION_LABELS is passed in as a parameter rather than moved, so the new module carries no page-level constants.

functions.name: describeUnavailable
functions.input: an internal reason string, the section key, whether satellite analysis ran, and the section description
functions.output: a label, a plain-English detail sentence, and one of five tones
functions.if_none: an unrecognised or absent reason returns the error tone with a retry sentence, never a claim that the field was not part of the brief

functions.name: sectionDesc
functions.input: an optional section key string looked up against SECTION_LABELS
functions.output: that section's human description, used to make a 'no' explain what was checked
functions.if_none: returns undefined and the copy falls back to generic wording such as 'this layer'

values.nullable: no — every branch returns a non-empty string, asserted by test
values.guard_at: rendered only when non-empty and different from u.label
values.if_missing: the label alone renders, exactly as before this change

values.nullable: yes — an unknown section key yields undefined
values.guard_at: optional chaining plus a truthiness check on the section key itself
values.if_missing: wording degrades to 'this layer' rather than throwing or printing undefined

break_it.scenario: A checked-clear field renders while the reader cannot tell whether anything was checked
break_it.what_happens: 'None here' alone reads identically whether the layer was queried and came back empty or was never queried at all
break_it.how: the detail sentence now renders beneath the label, and it states what was checked
break_it.repro: Open /reports/intelligence-brief for an address with a clear overlay result: the field must read 'None here' followed by the sentence naming what was checked, not the label alone.

break_it.scenario: A future branch is added to describeUnavailable with a label but no explanation
break_it.what_happens: The field would silently regress to a bare status word, reintroducing exactly this defect
break_it.how: brief-unavailable-copy.test.ts asserts every branch, across five sections and fourteen reason strings, returns a detail of at least five words that differs from its label

break_it.scenario: The copy is moved again and the source-scan guards keep passing over a file that no longer holds it
break_it.what_happens: Every not.toContain assertion in brief-copy-guards.test.ts would pass vacuously, protecting nothing
break_it.how: the guard now scans page.tsx and unavailable.ts concatenated, so the copy is found wherever it lives; a missing unavailable.ts throws on readFileSync rather than passing quietly

break_it.scenario: A long detail sentence overflows a narrow grid cell on mobile
break_it.what_happens: Text could clip or force horizontal scroll in the four-column field grid
break_it.how: the detail renders in a paragraph carrying break-words and overflow-wrap anywhere, the same treatment the normal field value already uses
break_it.repro: Open /reports/intelligence-brief at a 375px viewport on a section with an unavailable satellite layer and confirm the sentence wraps inside its cell.

mutation_analysis: Rewriting the not-requested branch's detail to the bare label 'Not included' turned two assertions red (2 failed / 7 passed) and restoring the sentence returned all nine to green, so the explanation assertions are not vacuous. The extraction itself is covered by the full suite: 82 suites / 1,095 tests pass, and tsc reports zero errors, which is what catches a bad move of a 135-line block. The React rendering of u.detail is asserted by a source-scan guard rather than a render test — a mutation that deleted the JSX but left the string in the file would not be caught.
residual_risk: The per-field JSX is still verified by source scanning, not by rendering the component, because page.tsx remains a single large client component. The lot_dimensions and heritage formatters noted in the previous change remain untested for the same reason. Extracting the field renderer is the next step if this area is touched again.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — regenerate an Intelligence Brief for an address with at least one empty field and confirm each empty field shows both the short label and the sentence explaining what was or was not checked; check a satellite layer left unticked reads as an instruction to tick and re-run, not as a finding.
